text:
Leah Gomez: customer escalation — streaming SSE sessions intermittently close with a 429 mid-stream. They report their UI shows ~1.9k tokens for a session but our ledger for the same session shows ~1.0k. They attached raw SSE transcript and say reconnections sometimes create duplicated fragments.

Omar Aziz: thanks Leah. Which transport are they using and any request-id?

Leah Gomez: Node http2 client. Header X-Req-ID: xr-77f6. Account acct-7742. Attached curl repro (redacted key):

```
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "X-Req-ID: xr-77f6" \
  "https://api.redwood.example/v1/outputs?model=redwood-lite&stream=true&max_tokens=5000" \
  --data '{"prompt":"<very long prompt>","stream":true}'
```

Heather Li: pulled edge logs for xr-77f6. We see chunks sent then a rate_limit event injected, then connection close: 

```
[2026-04-01T18:14:02Z] xr-77f6 conn=px-22 send_chunk id=ch-21 tokens=480
[2026-04-01T18:14:08Z] xr-77f6 conn=px-22 send_chunk id=ch-22 tokens=512
[2026-04-01T18:14:12Z] rate_limiter deny key=acct-7742 reason=burst_exhausted window=60s
[2026-04-01T18:14:12Z] xr-77f6 conn=px-22 write_event event=rate_limit data=429
[2026-04-01T18:14:12Z] xr-77f6 conn=px-22 connection_close by=proxy reason=rate_limit
```

Heather Li: proxy transcript includes actual SSE payloads:

```
id: 21
event: token
data: {"chunk_id":"ch-21","tokens":480}

id: 22
event: token
data: {"chunk_id":"ch-22","tokens":512}

event: rate_limit
data: 429

--- connection closed ---
```

Omar Aziz: ledger shows only ch-21 committed (480 tokens). ch-22 not in ledger. Client claims it received both and shows ~2k tokens total. So client saw tokens that weren't billed.

infra-bot: auto-ticket created: STREAM-429-7742, severity=medium, tags=[eng-runtime, eng-infra, billing].

Leah Gomez: customer impact: they want to reconcile the invoice immediately. Also worried about duplicates on reconnect.

Omar Aziz: quick analysis: two separate timing issues together: (A) prebuffering/prefetch at the proxy allows us to write chunks to the socket before we persist them to billing; (B) rate-limiter triggers on a quota check that runs slightly later, so we inject rate_limit + close. If TCP already delivered bytes to client, client will render them but ledger hasn't been updated.

Heather Li: hypothesis validated on local harness. Repro: enable_proxy_prefetch=3 -> delivered_to_client > ledger when limiter trips. With enable_proxy_prefetch=0 ledger and client counts align but you still hit 429s (just no mismatch).

Leah Gomez: customer reconnect behavior: they use Last-Event-ID on reconnect. Their code appends chunks into a buffer and does not de-duplicate chunk_id, so duplicates appear when both server delivers the chunk again after reconnection.

Omar Aziz: short-term mitigation options:
- Support guidance: ask customer to set client to de-duplicate by chunk_id, ensure Last-Event-ID is sent on reconnect, and optionally reduce client-side parallel prefetch (if their client supports it).
- Platform quickfix: set 'proxy.prefetch_window=0' for acct-7742 and any other flagged accounts.
- Billing: open a reconciliation ticket and promise to audit session before adjustments. Do not promise credits until engineering audit confirms.

billing-bot: ledger note: acct-7742 session xr-77f6 shows 480 tokens billed. Recon ticket BG-7742 created for potential backfill.

Heather Li: proposed engineering fixes (short/mid/long):
- short: enable per-chunk idempotent commits in billing-writer behind a feature flag. When a chunk is queued, write or reserve with chunk_id so ledger can reflect it immediately. Backfill for recent sessions flagged.
- mid: modify rate-limiter to reserve quota on chunk enqueue instead of on final accounting; maintain reservation TTL to release if not committed. This avoids emitting chunks client-side that aren't reflected in quota.
- long: change SSE close behavior to send a 'stream_end' event with a last_committed_offset and to treat rate_limit events as advisory with retry-after payload instead of abrupt close, giving clients a chance to pause gracefully.

infra-bot: planned change: rollout toggle proxy.prefetch_window=0 for acct-7742 at 2026-04-01T22:00Z, rollout id roll-9843.

Leah Gomez: draft customer message (non-technical):

"Hi — thanks for reporting. We see evidence that a rate limit was enforced during your streaming session which, due to temporary prefetch behavior at our edge, could have allowed some output to reach your client before our billing system finalized the session. We're applying a temporary configuration change to eliminate prefetch for your account and will audit the session. If we find delivered content that wasn't billed, we'll make adjustments and follow up. Please send your raw SSE transcript and tcpdump so we can correlate; also, if possible, enable Last-Event-ID and chunk_id-based de-duplication in your client.

We don't expect new charges because of this report while we're investigating. We'll update you within 48 hours with next steps"

Omar Aziz: wording tweak: avoid "don't expect new charges" maybe say "we will not make billing adjustments without completing an audit". Legal reviewed? keep conservative.

Leah Gomez: updated message sent. Asked customer for raw artifacts and confirmed we've scheduled proxy toggle.

Heather Li: I ran quick test with 'proxy.prefetch_window=0' in staging — ledger matches client in my tests even when limiter trips. So short-term fix seems effective.

Omar Aziz: action items:
- (Heather) enable per-chunk feature-flag in billing-writer prototype and run canary on internal accounts.
- (Infra) apply proxy.prefetch_window=0 for acct-7742 (infra-bot scheduled).
- (Leah) collect customer tcpdump and SSE transcript; coordinate billing audit.
- (Eng) design reservation-based limiter (mid-term).

billing-bot: follow-up ticket BG-7742 assigned to billing ops.

Leah Gomez: marking P2. If we see >3 accounts with same pattern escalate to incidents channel. Thanks team :thumbsup:

infra-bot: STATUS UPDATE: roll-9843 applied to acct-7742 at 2026-04-01T22:00Z. Monitoring metric: stream_mismatch_count.

Omar Aziz: closing the loop here for now. Keep this thread open for any further artifacts from the customer.
